name: Melkodige Estate Saccharomyces 72hrs Naturals
description:
Tastes Like  -   Pomegranate, Pink Guava and Golden Raisins 
 
 Roasting Profile     -    Filter ( Light Roast )  
 
 
 Process     -    Saccharomyces 72hrs Naturals 
 
   Varietal -  Sl 9  
   Altitude -  1280 MASL    
   Producer Name     -  Aveen and Yogita Rodrigues   
   Harvest Year   -  2025  
 
     Coffee Producers Note  -       R  ed, fully ripe cherries with a Brix level above 22 are selectively handpicked and carefully cleaned using a water bath to remove impurities and lighter fruit. The cherries then undergo anaerobic fermentation in sealed drums for 72 hours, allowing complex flavours to develop. 
 Post-fermentation, they are transferred to raised wooden drying beds and dried slowly under shade nets. During this stage, the cherries are regularly raked to ensure even and consistent drying. Once fully dried, they are packed into gunny bags and rested for 60 days, allowing the flavours to stabilise and mature before further processing. 
      Roasters Note  -      We’ve taken this coffee light to preserve its vibrancy and showcase the fruit character developed during fermentation. Expect a bright, expressive cup with juicy acidity and a clean, lingering sweetness. In the cup: Pomegranate leads with a fresh, winey brightness, followed by soft pink guava and a rounded golden raisin sweetness on the finish. The body is smooth and supple, with a crisp yet balanced aftertaste. Best enjoyed when brewed clean and slightly cooler to let the fruit open up gradually.

name: Salawara Estate Bioreactor Naturals
description:
Tastes Like  -   Spiced Mandarin Tea , Dried Apple and Cranberry  
 
 Roasting Profile     -    Filter ( Light Roast )  
 
 
 Process     -    Naturals 
 
   Varietal -  SL 795  
   Altitude -   1050 MASL   
   Producer Name     -   Mr. Sharan Gowda   
   Harvest Year   -  2025  
 
     Coffee Producers Note  -     This lot was fermented in our newly introduced bioreactor, a state-of-the-art fermentation system designed to ensure precise control and homogeneous fermentation. The coffees were placed in the bioreactor for 72 hours, where temperature, oxygen levels, and microbial activity were carefully managed. A specially selected yeast strain was introduced during fermentation to enhance and amplify the fruit-forward characteristics of the coffee. Once fermentation was complete, the coffee was removed from the bioreactor and dried slowly on raised beds, allowing the developed flavors to stabilize and fully express themselves in the final cup.  
      Roasters Note  -       This coffee is a beautiful example of controlled fermentation done right. Processed in a state-of-the-art bioreactor over 72 hours with carefully managed temperature, oxygen, and a selected yeast strain, the result is an exceptionally clean yet expressive cup. Roasted for filter to highlight clarity and sweetness, it opens up with a vibrant spiced mandarin tea character, followed by layers of dried apple and a crisp cranberry finish. Bright, fruit-forward, and structured , a lot that feels both lively and refined.

name: Salawara Estate Carbonic Maceration
description:
Tastes Like  -    Watermelon, Orange Blossom, and Damson Plum          
 
 
 Roasting Profile     -    Filter ( Light Roast )  
 
 
 Process     -    Carbonic Maceration Naturals  
 
   Varietal -   SL 795 + SL 6   
   Altitude -   1050 MASL   
   Producer Name     -   Mr. Sharan Gowda   
   Harvest Year   -  2025  
 
     Coffee Producers Note  -     Ripe coffee cherries are carefully handpicked from  Dodda kere Patte, at a Brix level of 24. The cherries are then sealed in stainless steel tanks and pressurized with carbon dioxide for 72 hours, creating an anaerobic environment that initiates carbonic maceration. During this stage, intracellular fermentation occurs within the intact cherries, intensifying fruit-forward characteristics and enhancing aromatic complexity. After fermentation, the cherries are removed from the tanks and slowly dried on raised beds, preserving clarity, sweetness, and vibrant fruity flavors in the cup.  
      Roasters Note  -      We roasted this carbonic maceration lot with a focus on clarity and fruit expression. The profile brings out its watermelon-like juiciness and orange blossom aromatics, supported by a deeper damson plum sweetness. Development was kept controlled to retain acidity and structure while preserving a light, refreshing finish.
tasting_notes: Watermelon, Stone Fruit like Plum & Vibrant Acidity ||

name: Salawara Estate Mosto fermentation
description:
Tastes Like  -   White peach, Golden Raisin and Bergamot 
 
 Roasting Profile     -    Filter ( Light Roast )  
 
 
 Process     -    Champagne Fermentation 
 
   Varietal -  SL 795  
   Altitude -   1050 MASL   
   Producer Name     -   Mr. Sharan Gowda   
   Harvest Year   -  2024-2025  
 
     Coffee Producers Note  -     “Mosto” refers to the sweet, fermented juice extracted from coffee cherries or their mucilage, rich in natural sugars, acids, and a diverse microbial culture of yeasts and bacteria. Fresh coffee cherries are placed in large, food-grade barrels, and “musto” from a previous batch of natural coffees is added to accelerate fermentation and enhance complexity. The coffees are then slow-dried using a nursery-style drying method.  
      Roasters Note  -      In the cup, expect a delicate interplay of white peach and golden raisin, bringing a soft, rounded sweetness, while bergamot lifts the profile with a fragrant, citrusy brightness. The acidity is elegant with a silky mouthfeel and a clean, lingering finish. The nursery-style drying further refines the structure of the cup, preserving aromatics while enhancing sweetness and balance. A refined and aromatic profile. ideal for those who enjoy floral, fruit-forward coffees with a composed fermentation character.

name: Salawara Estate Pichia Fermentation HSD
description:
Tastes Like  -   Green Apple, Prune and Creamy Mouthfeel  
 
 Roasting Profile     -    Filter ( Light Roast )  
 
 
 Process     -    Honey Sun Dried 
 
   Varietal -  SL 6 + SL 9  
   Altitude -   1050 MASL   
   Producer Name     -   Mr. Sharan Gowda   
   Harvest Year   -  2024-2025  
 
     Coffee Producers Note  -     The coffees were harvested from Block 24 at a Brix level of 22. This lot underwent yeast inoculation using Pichia and Lactobacillus, fermented in large stainless-steel tanks. Carbon dioxide was introduced during fermentation to enhance the coffee’s fruity flavour profile. The coffee was then processed using the natural method and slow-dried for 22 days in a controlled nursery drying system.  
      Roasters Note  -      This lot shows a bright green-apple acidity layered over prune-like sweetness. We roasted it to keep those fruit tones intact while allowing the creamy mouthfeel to carry through on the finish. Development was kept controlled to retain clarity and balance without compromising texture, making it suited for both filter and modern espresso styles.

name: SCA Brewing Foundation Course
description:
The Brewing Foundation course offers a comprehensive introduction to the art and science of coffee brewing. Through both theory and hands-on practice, learners are guided through various brewing methods using a range of devices. 
 This course is ideal for beginners and provides the fundamental skills and knowledge needed to craft delicious brewed coffee.  
  Time:  10:30 AM - 6:30 PM 
  Location:  Corridor Seven Coffee Academy [ Map Link ] 
  What You'll Learn:    
  1. Coffee Knowledge :  Understand Arabica vs. Robusta, processing methods, and best practices for coffee storage. 
  2. Brewing Methods & Equipment :  Explore manual brewers like V60, French Press, and AeroPress, and learn how to use essential brewing tools. 
  3. Brewing Guidelines :  Master the 7 key elements of brewing: ratio, grind, time, temperature, turbulence, water quality, and filter type. 
  4. Brewing Techniques :  Practice percolation (V60), immersion (French Press), and hybrid (AeroPress) brewing styles. 
  5. Brew Analysis :  Learn to evaluate your brew by analyzing its color, aroma, taste, and body. 
  6. Equipment Maintenance :  Maintain your brewing tools for consistency, cleanliness, and long-term performance. 
 With a strong focus on practical application, participants will learn how to brew thoughtfully, evaluate their results, and make informed adjustments. The course concludes with a written assessment to test your grasp of the foundational concepts. 
  Who Should Enroll  
 The SCA Brewing Foundation course is designed for: 
 -  Home Brewers  eager to explore the world of coffee at home 
 -  Aspiring Baristas  and individuals interested in building a career in the food and beverage industry 
  Course Outcome  
 Participants who complete both the  practical exam during the course  and the  online written exam  afterward will receive the  SCA Brewing Foundation Certificate , an internationally recognized credential that also contributes toward the SCA Coffee Diploma .  
  Course Fee  
 INR 23,600 (inclusive of GST) 
  Fee Included  
 - Access to the globally respected SCA coffee education system 
 - Comprehensive course materials and reference notes 
 - Certification upon successful completion of all assessments and exams. 
  Certification:  
 Upon successful completion of both the practical and theoretical exams, participants will receive the  SCA Brewing Foundation Certificate.  
  About the Trainer  
  Naitik Shah  grew up in Muscat, Oman, where an early exposure to café culture sparked his passion for coffee. He now leads the coffee program at  Corridor Seven Coffee Roasters  and is a certified  SCA Authorized Trainer (AST)  in Brewing.

His teaching blends global standards with real-world insights—perfect for anyone looking to build a solid foundation in specialty coffee.

 - Small batch classes for focused learning

 - A supportive space to ask questions, taste widely, and grow confidently in coffee knowledge 
 - Part of the broader Coffee Skills Program that includes advanced modules in Brewing, and more
